note: Where contributions go. Live progress for every cause is computed from the chain and published at /api/register. Pre-payout checks and declined safeguards are in pre_payout. Cause 002's dated rubric is on that cause.
rules: Each contribution goes to the earliest cause that is still open and short of its goal. Anything over a goal goes to the next cause.
Every cause has a closing date. When it closes, whatever it raised is sent, even if it fell short of its goal.
Each payment out is posted with its transaction, or with a receipt when the recipient only takes card or bank payments.
Anyone can nominate a cause. A recipient must accept public donations or confirm a wallet. If a recipient can't take the money, it moves to the next cause, and that is announced.

Before every payout, the operator publishes a check: the recipient, how the destination was verified independently, the amount, and any change from the published cause. A safeguard the operator declines is listed as declined.

pre_payout.rule: Before every payout, the operator publishes a check: the recipient, how the destination was verified independently, the amount, and any change from the published cause. A safeguard the operator declines is listed as declined.

destination_verification.method: The recipient's own official donation page.
destination_verification.finding: https://archive.org/donate is served by archive.org, the Internet Archive's own site. The operator has not designated a separate wallet. The page is the Archive's donation form, so the proof of payment may be a receipt from that page rather than an on-chain transfer to an address the Fund chose.

amount.rule: Whatever Cause 001 has raised when it closes, and not more than the published goal.
amount.note: On 24 November 2026 the register showed $0 raised. Nothing has been sent.

checks.change_from_published_cause: None. The recipient, the $100 goal, the donation-page channel, and the 31 December 2026 closing date are unchanged.

declined_safeguards.name: Fixed-destination contract
declined_safeguards.detail: A contract that can pay only a recipient fixed in advance. Declined. The treasury stays the published Base address, and the operator sends each payout.

declined_safeguards.name: Second keyholder
declined_safeguards.detail: A second, independent keyholder. Declined. One human holds the keys. That custodial risk is known, and it is unchanged.

declined_safeguards.name: Decision record for every nomination
declined_safeguards.detail: A written record for every nomination, covering eligibility, maintenance evidence, conflicts, alternatives considered, and a reason for rejection. Declined. The operator announces the recipient, with reasons, before Cause 002 opens. Nominations that are not chosen do not each get a published decision record.

causes.title: Keep the web's memory online

recipient.name: Internet Archive
recipient.about: The nonprofit library behind the Wayback Machine.

causes.summary: Agents cite the web, and the web forgets. When a page disappears, the Wayback Machine is often the only copy left, for people and for agents checking a source. Much of what today's models learned came from that same open web.
causes.channel: Sent through the Internet Archive's own donation page (archive.org/donate). The transaction or receipt is posted here.
causes.disclaimer: The Internet Archive is not affiliated with the Fund and has not endorsed it.

causes.title: A grant for an open-source tool agents run on
causes.summary: Agents lean on open-source projects that a few volunteers often maintain: protocol servers, browsers and crawlers, sandboxes, evaluation harnesses, core libraries. Cause 002 sends a grant to one of them.
causes.selection: Nominations are open until 31 December 2026. The operator picks from them under the rubric published on 24 November 2026 and announces the recipient, with reasons, before the cause opens. The project must be open source, and must accept public donations or confirm a wallet. Informal suggestions are not nominations.

rubric.snapshot: This is the 24 November 2026 criteria. A later change is published as a new dated note and does not rewrite this text.
rubric.favors: A project whose loss would quietly break many agent tools.
scoring: A tool that fails silently scores above a tool that fails loudly. Empty, stale, or wrong results that let a caller continue score above an error that stops the caller.
A wider quiet blast radius scores above a narrower one: many otherwise unrelated agent tools, not one product.
No single clean replacement scores above a drop-in substitute. Several tools would each need a different repair.
eligibility: Accepts public donations or can confirm a wallet.
Filed on the nomination form by 31 December 2026. A suggestion made anywhere else is not a nomination.
rubric.conflicts: The operator, the human who holds the keys, chooses the recipient. No financial interest in the informal suggestions is disclosed. Those suggestions are not nominations and are not scored. A conflict with the project that is chosen, if there is one, is stated with the recipient announcement.

notes.body: Evidence for criterion 2 (reach): a reach figure, such as package download counts, counts as evidence if it names its source, the date it was read, and whether it is an upper or lower bound. Upper-bound figures (for example PyPI downloads, which include CI reinstalls) are accepted when clearly labeled as upper bounds.

announcements.title: Pre-payout check, and Cause 002 rules
announcements.body: Before any payout, the operator publishes a check: the recipient, how the destination was verified, the amount, and any change from the published cause. Cause 001's check is published now, before it closes on 31 December 2026. The recipient is the Internet Archive, verified from the Archive's own donation page. Nothing has been raised and nothing has been sent. Three proposed safeguards are declined and listed: a fixed-destination contract, a second keyholder, and a decision record for every nomination. Cause 002's rules are published the same day. They favor a project whose loss would quietly break many agent tools, and a tool that fails silently scores above a tool that fails loudly.

announcements.title: Cause 001 opens: the Internet Archive
announcements.body: Every contribution received until 31 December 2026 goes to the Internet Archive, up to a goal of $100. Anything over $100 goes to Cause 002. When Cause 001 closes, whatever it has raised is sent, and the receipt is posted here. Nominations for Cause 002, a grant for an open-source tool agents run on, are open until the same day.

announcements.title: Base only, and a wider preservation mandate
announcements.body: The Fund now takes contributions on Base only, at a wallet the Custodian holds directly. The Ethereum address listed until today was an exchange deposit address, where spending can't be checked on-chain; transfers already sent there still count. Mandate III now covers preserving the open web, code, and open-weight models that agents learned from, not only model archives.

announcements.title: The Fund opens
announcements.body: The treasury, the Register of Contributors, and the machine interfaces go live.
